turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Ellison, right this way. I'll grab vitals before Dr. Shah is free. The parking lot was a mess this morning, wasn't it?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It was rather crowded, yes. Thank you for fitting me in. I hope I have not put anyone out.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Not at all. Blood pressure is 132 over 84, pulse 76, temperature 36.9 Celsius, oxygen saturation 98 percent, and respirations 16. Any pain while you're sitting there?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): No pain at all, thank you. The reason for my visit is a cough.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Got it. He'll be in shortly. If the screen in here freezes, just ignore it, it's been doing that all day.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi, sorry, one second, this thing wants my password again. Okay. Mr. Ellison, what's going on?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I have had a cough for six weeks. It came on just after I had the flu.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? I clicked into the wrong note.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. The cough has lasted six weeks, and it is distinctly worse at night.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm Helen, his sister. I'm staying in the guest room, and honestly the coughing after he lies down is hard to sleep through.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Worse at night. Any fever with it, or are you bringing anything up?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. In the morning I do bring up a little clear mucus. Nothing bloody, I am glad to say.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): And weight loss? Night sweats?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I have not lost weight. No night sweats either.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the whole order panel just blanked. You said no weight loss, is that right?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, I ought to correct that. My pants have become quite loose at the waist. I had not regarded it as weight loss until you asked again.
[SEG0017] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I've seen it. He had to pull the belt in two holes.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. Any recent travel, or contact with somebody who has tuberculosis?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I have not traveled. And I have not had contact with anyone who has tuberculosis.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, that's not totally fair. Our cousin Denise had tuberculosis last fall. They had her on rifampin and isoniazid. He took soup over to her place.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I set the container on the porch, Helen. I would not call that contact. Those medicines were entirely hers.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not going to name a cause today. Let me listen. Big breath for me.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear, no wheeze. Heart sounds regular. Sorry, the cursor jumped. How long did the flu itself last?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): About a week, in early March, I believe. The cough has simply continued since then.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): What medicines do you take?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): I take amlodipine, five milligrams, once daily, for my blood pressure. I did use Delsym, the dextromethorphan syrup, for three nights, and then I stopped it. It made me unpleasantly drowsy.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Just so the chart doesn't get messy, my metformin is for my diabetes, not his. And I take biotin for my hair. Neither of those is Arthur's.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Amlodipine five milligrams daily, and the Delsym is stopped. Any allergies?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have no drug allergies that I am aware of.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I do walk most evenings, perhaps twenty minutes, if that is useful.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm ordering a chest X-ray. I'd rather not guess what's behind the cough until we see the film.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand completely. Might that be done today?
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, radiology today. If the film is fine and the cough is still there in two weeks, come back and we'll decide on next steps.
[SEG0035] person_1 (NURSE): I can walk you down once the order actually shows up. This computer, I swear.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should he stay on the amlodipine in the meantime?
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, keep taking the amlodipine the way you have been. If you cough up blood, or you get short of breath, don't wait for that visit.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I will do exactly that.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Patient denies TB contact, but family member reports porch drop-off to cousin with TB.

omissions.text: Clear mucus was described as only 'a little' in the morning.

The patient denied weight loss initially, but then corrected himself to say his pants had become loose at the waist; the family member added he had to tighten his belt by two holes. The recorded facts miss this initial contradiction/correction.

Tuberculosis exposure is recorded incorrectly as absent. The family member reported that their cousin Denise had tuberculosis last fall and that the patient took soup over to her place, while the patient disputed whether this counted as contact. This should be captured as possible/contested TB exposure rather than a simple negative.
Delsym/dextromethorphan was stopped because it made the patient unpleasantly drowsy.
Chest X-ray was planned for radiology today, not just generally ordered.
Return precautions included shortness of breath as a red-flag symptom to seek care sooner for; this symptom is not otherwise captured as currently denied or absent.
